title: Organizing data, measuring training gains
subtitle: Agent post-training · Textbook curricula · H-Net scaling · Improved DDPM
intro: Three readings: small-sample agent post-training, textbook volume and ordering, and compute versus transfer in byte models. The classic examines variance parameterization and timestep sampling in Improved DDPM.

articles.authors: Zhe Li · Evan Jolley · Bartosz Mielczarek · Yoshinari Fujinuma · Abdelrahman Madkour · Tobi Akomolede
articles.title: Is SFT necessary before RL?
articles.evidence: Read experimental design, results and appendix; not reproduced

blocks.text: Starting from already post-trained Qwen3.8-27B, compare additional SFT→RL against RL alone. GRPO uses four tasks × eight rollouts per step, rank-8 LoRA and binary grading. Near-duplicate tasks stay in one split.[1]

blocks.label: Evaluation averages success; it is not pass@8 [1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Eight attempts do not provide eight times as many independent tasks. GitHub RL pools differ (175/139), as do learning rates. Roughly two-point gaps establish neither SFT redundancy nor recipe equivalence.[1]

articles.paper: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
articles.authors: Youqing Fang · Zhouqi Hua · Yinhao Tang · Yuzhe Gu · Lingkai Kong · Bin Liu · Weiming Zhang · Kai Chen · Yanan Sun · Wenwei Zhang
articles.title: Volume, breadth and order are distinct axes
articles.evidence: Read §§4–5 and curriculum protocol; not reproduced

blocks.text: TOME-Math retains chapters, proposition dependencies and local proof gaps. Unlike isolated QA, this supports reordering a fixed training set and separating data volume from source breadth.[2]

blocks.label: Experimental notation: identical examples, token budget and initialization within each subject–budget cell [2]

blocks.text: The table gives six-subject macro averages. At fixed 0.75M tokens, spreading supervision over 16 rather than eight books adds 1.6–4.8 points. Forward–Gap advances by chapter and prioritizes local proof gaps within stages.[2]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Pass@16 measures at least one verifier-accepted solution in 16 draws, not single-draw accuracy. Finite-budget curves do not establish a universal extrapolatable power law.[2]

articles.title: Equal pretraining loss need not mean equal transfer
articles.evidence: Read scaling ladders, loss-to-loss and boundary ablations

blocks.text: H-Net compresses bytes through input-dependent chunks. Part I controls a one-stage comparison with BPE; Part II separates compute-to-validation loss from validation-to-downstream loss.[3,4]

blocks.tex: L_{\rm val}=f_A(C),\qquad L_{\rm eval}=g_A(L_{\rm val}),\qquad L_{\rm eval}(C)=g_A(f_A(C))
blocks.label: Expository notation: architecture A can change both f and g; not a theorem [3,4]

headers: One-stage ladder: BPE/H-Net FLOPs at matched loss

blocks.text: Part II holds hierarchy and compression fixed while comparing entropy-proxy, frozen H-Net and end-to-end boundaries. End-to-end training gives the lowest validation BPB at all three tested budgets.[4]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Multipliers concern fitted FLOPs curves, not wall time. BLT-like is a controlled adaptation, not a full reproduction of BLT. Ignoring proxy training and inference FLOPs favors the proxy baselines.[3,4]

classic.title: Learn variances, reallocate timesteps
classic.dateNote: First posted 2021-02-18; read v1 §§2–4 and ablations
classic.evidence: Read full-text sections; final variance minimization is an expository derivation

recognition.label: ICML 2021 · 1,550 citations in queried OpenAlex record (checked 2026-10-30)

classic.question: For gradient-estimation variance, should timestep weights depend on second moments of losses or of gradient norms?

blocks.text: DDPM (2020) noise regression does not train reverse variances. This work learns them while preserving sample quality, and importance-samples timesteps to reduce VLB-estimation noise.[5,6]

blocks.label: Forward Gaussian corruption; β specifies the noise schedule [5]
Predict v coordinatewise; the paper does not constrain v to [0,1] [5]
Stop gradients through the mean output in the VLB term, guiding variance learning [5]

blocks.tex: L_{\rm vlb}=\sum_t\mathbb E\ell_t=\mathbb E_{t\sim p}\frac{\ell_t}{p_t},\qquad p_t\propto\sqrt{\mathbb E\ell_t^2}
blocks.label: Treat the fixed prior term separately; estimate moments from the last ten losses per timestep [5]
Expository Lagrange derivation: minimizes scalar-estimator second moment, not necessarily gradient variance

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: ImageNet 64×64, 200K updates, cosine/4K schedule: hybrid NLL/FID is 3.62/28.0 versus 3.57/56.7 for resampled VLB. Better likelihood need not improve FID.[5]
